StepTransitions.Description: Directed control-flow edges represented as first-class pko:Transition instances with fromStep/toStep and next/alternative/fallback semantics.

schema.name: StepTransitionId
schema.Description: Stored logical identifier for one StepTransitions row.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Human-readable calculated display alias for the StepTransitions row.

schema.name: ProcedureVersion
schema.Description: Procedure version whose control flow owns the transition.

schema.name: FromStep
schema.Description: Source step; maps to pko:fromStep.

schema.name: ToStep
schema.Description: Destination step; maps to pko:toStep.

schema.name: TransitionKind
schema.Description: Next, Alternative, or Fallback.

schema.name: Condition
schema.Description: Condition under which the edge is taken.

schema.name: Priority
schema.Description: Evaluation priority when several outgoing edges exist.

schema.name: IsRecoveryPath
schema.Description: TRUE when this transition is a non-default path taken because something went wrong.

schema.name: CountOfFromStepExecutions
schema.Description: How many times the step this transition leaves from has actually been executed.

schema.name: CountOfToStepExecutions
schema.Description: How many times the step this transition arrives at has actually been executed.

schema.name: HasReachableOrigin
schema.Description: TRUE when the origin step of this transition has been executed at least once.

schema.name: HasReachableTarget
schema.Description: TRUE when the destination step of this transition has been executed at least once.

schema.name: IsNeverExercised
schema.Description: TRUE when at least one end of this transition has never appeared in any step execution.

schema.name: IsUntestedRecoveryPath
schema.Description: TRUE for a Fallback or Alternative transition whose endpoints show no execution evidence.

schema.name: CountOfObservedTraversals
schema.Description: How many times this exact transition has actually been traversed.

schema.name: HasBeenTraversed
schema.Description: TRUE when this transition has been walked at least once.

schema.name: IsUnwalkedRecoveryPath
schema.Description: TRUE for a Fallback/Alternative transition with zero recorded traversals.

schema.name: TargetBlockingRequirementCount
schema.Description: How many blocking requirements are attached to the step this transition lands on.

schema.name: TargetCarriesBlockingControl
schema.Description: Whether the destination step of this transition carries at least one blocking control.

schema.name: IsUnrehearsedControlEntry
schema.Description: A recovery path that has never been traversed and that leads into a step carrying a blocking control.

schema.name: UnrehearsedControlVersionKey
schema.Description: Composite-key echo: this transition's procedure version when it is an unrehearsed control entry, blank otherwise.

schema.name: LeadsToClosure
schema.Description: Transitive closure of the step graph (FromStep -> ToStep over every transition kind), materialized by each substrate as vw_step_transitions_closure: every (from, to) pair a procedure can lead to in one or more transitions. A step that lies on a cycle reaches itself.

schema.name: FromStepIsHumanApprovalGate
schema.Description: This transition leaves a human approval gate.

schema.name: ToStepIsHumanApprovalGate
schema.Description: This transition enters a human approval gate.

schema.name: AvoidsHumanApprovalGate
schema.Description: Neither end of this transition is a human approval gate, so a route made only of such transitions never passes a gate.

schema.name: LeadsWithoutHumanGateClosure
schema.Description: Transitive closure of the step graph over only the transitions that avoid every human approval gate, materialized as vw_step_transitions_closure_where_avoids_human_approval_gate: every (from, to) pair a procedure can reach without passing a gate.

schema.name: SemanticTypeIri
schema.Description: Exact PKO class IRI.

schema.name: DecisionPointCount
schema.Description: Decision points that select this transition.

schema.name: IsUndocumentedBranch
schema.Description: TRUE for an alternative or fallback branch no decision point explains.

Requirements.Description: Normative requirements applied to procedures, steps, or transitions. Maps to pko:Requirement and pko:hasRequirement.

schema.name: RequirementId
schema.Description: Stored logical identifier for one Requirements row.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Human-readable calculated display alias for the Requirements row.

schema.name: Label
schema.Description: Requirement label.

schema.name: RequirementType
schema.Description: Controlled requirement type; maps to pko:hasRequirementType.

schema.name: Statement
schema.Description: Normative requirement statement.

schema.name: Rationale
schema.Description: Why the requirement exists.

schema.name: IsBlocking
schema.Description: TRUE when unsatisfied requirement blocks execution or approval.

schema.name: SatisfactionRecordCount
schema.Description: How many times this requirement has ever been evaluated against an execution.

schema.name: StepBindingCount
schema.Description: How many steps the specification binds this requirement to.

schema.name: IsBoundToAnyStep
schema.Description: TRUE when at least one step carries this requirement.

schema.name: HasEverBeenEvaluated
schema.Description: TRUE when this requirement has at least one satisfaction record in the model.

schema.name: NegativeOutcomeCount
schema.Description: How many times this requirement has ever produced a less-than-satisfied outcome.

schema.name: IsInoperativeControl
schema.Description: TRUE for a blocking requirement that is attached to a step in the specification but has never once been evaluated on any execution.

schema.name: IsDecorativeControl
schema.Description: TRUE for a blocking requirement that is not attached to any step at all.

schema.name: HasComputedWitness
schema.Description: Whether a computed predicate in this rulebook evaluates this requirement, as opposed to it being satisfied by human assertion only.

schema.name: WitnessFieldName
schema.Description: The fully-qualified Table.Field of the predicate that computes this requirement, when one exists.

schema.name: HasEverProducedNegative
schema.Description: TRUE when this requirement has at least once been scored as anything other than Satisfied.

schema.name: IsUnfalsifiedControl
schema.Description: TRUE for a blocking control that HAS been evaluated at least once and has never returned a negative result.

schema.name: ClaimsAWitnessField
schema.Description: TRUE when this requirement names a field it claims computes it.

schema.name: NamedWitnessFieldExists
schema.Description: TRUE when the field named in WitnessFieldName actually exists in the field catalog AND is a derived (calculated/lookup/aggregation) field.

schema.name: DerivedHasComputedWitness
schema.Description: Whether this requirement genuinely has a computed witness, derived from the field catalog rather than asserted.

schema.name: WitnessClaimIsUnverified
schema.Description: TRUE when the hand-typed HasComputedWitness flag disagrees with what the field catalog says.

schema.name: IsUnwitnessedBlockingControl
schema.Description: TRUE for a blocking control with no verified computed witness behind it.

schema.name: WitnessFireCount
schema.Description: How many times this requirement's evaluation has returned a non-Satisfied result.

schema.name: WitnessHasNeverFired
schema.Description: TRUE for a requirement that has a computed witness which has never once returned a negative result.

schema.name: EvaluationSampleSize
schema.Description: How many times this requirement has been evaluated at all.

schema.name: HasMeaningfulSample
schema.Description: TRUE when this requirement has been evaluated often enough that a clean record is informative.

schema.name: MinimumSampleForAssurance
schema.Description: The number of clean evaluations this control must accumulate before its silence counts as evidence.

schema.name: IsUntestedWitness
schema.Description: TRUE for a witness that has never fired and has not been exercised enough for that silence to mean anything.

schema.name: IsEvidencedHoldingControl
schema.Description: TRUE for a witness that has never fired across a sample large enough for that to constitute evidence.

schema.name: ControlAssuranceState
schema.Description: One of Decorative, Inoperative, Asserted, Demonstrated, Holding, or Untested — the single control-health verdict for this requirement.

schema.name: UnexercisedBindingCount
schema.Description: How many of this control's step bindings have never been evaluated.

schema.name: WitnessIsPartiallyScoped
schema.Description: TRUE when a control has a computed witness but at least one of its step bindings has never been exercised by it.

schema.name: AccountableRole
schema.Description: The role answerable for this control operating as designed.

schema.name: AccountableAgent
schema.Description: The person currently holding the accountable role for this control.

schema.name: HasNamedOwner
schema.Description: TRUE when a role has been named as accountable for this control.

schema.name: IsOrphanedBlockingControl
schema.Description: TRUE for a blocking control with nobody named as accountable for it.

schema.name: IsUnwatchedAndUnowned
schema.Description: TRUE for a blocking control that nothing computes and nobody owns.

schema.name: AttestationExposureNote
schema.Description: States, per control, what kind of exposure attesting to it creates.
schema.formula: =IF(NOT({{IsBlocking}}), "", IF({{IsUnwatchedAndUnowned}}, "Unwatched and unowned: exposure defaults to the signatory.", IF({{IsOrphanedBlockingControl}}, "Witnessed but unowned: no named accountability.", IF(NOT({{HasComputedWitness}}), "Owned but unwitnessed: rests on human judgement.", ""))))

schema.name: UnwatchedUnownedFlag
schema.Description: Constant marker echoed when this control is both unwatched and unowned.

schema.name: ControlledTerm
schema.Description: Controlled vocabulary term this requirement's concept maps to, if any.

schema.name: UsesControlledVocabulary
schema.Description: TRUE when this requirement points at a controlled term instead of only free-texting the concept.

schema.name: SemanticTypeIri
schema.Description: Exact PKO class IRI.

schema.name: RegulatoryFramework
schema.Description: Regulation that imposes the requirement.

schema.name: IsRegulatoryRequirement
schema.Description: TRUE when a regulation imposes the requirement.

schema.name: ConstraintTraceCount
schema.Description: Traces of this requirement as a constraint.

schema.name: IsUntracedBoundConstraint
schema.Description: TRUE when a constraint bound to a step traces to no collection activity.

data.Label: Close cutoff enforced
data.Statement: No ledger entry may be posted after cutoff without controller-approved reopening.
data.Rationale: SOX control design
data.Name: Close cutoff enforced
data.AttestationExposureNote: Witnessed but unowned: no named accountability.

data.Label: Reconciled balance integrity
data.Statement: Every material account must reconcile or carry an approved exception.
data.Rationale: Financial reporting accuracy
data.Name: Reconciled balance integrity
data.AttestationExposureNote: Witnessed but unowned: no named accountability.

data.Label: Preparer/approver separation
data.Statement: The preparer may not be the final approver.
data.Rationale: Segregation of duties
data.Name: Preparer/approver separation
data.AttestationExposureNote: Witnessed but unowned: no named accountability.

data.Label: Evidence retention
data.Statement: Evidence must remain retrievable for 7 years.
data.Rationale: Audit and legal retention
data.Name: Evidence retention
data.AttestationExposureNote: Witnessed but unowned: no named accountability.

data.Label: Human final approval
data.Statement: Controller and CFO approvals must be human-confirmed.
data.Rationale: Accountability
data.Name: Human final approval
data.AttestationExposureNote: Unwatched and unowned: exposure defaults to the signatory.

data.Label: Approved source only
data.Statement: Drafting may use only approved source resources and validated elicitation records.
data.Rationale: Semantic integrity
data.Name: Approved source only
data.AttestationExposureNote: Unwatched and unowned: exposure defaults to the signatory.

data.Label: Legal review required
data.Statement: Employment counsel must approve legal and privacy commitments.
data.Rationale: Legal accountability
data.Name: Legal review required
data.AttestationExposureNote: Unwatched and unowned: exposure defaults to the signatory.

data.Label: Human meaning approval
data.Statement: An AI agent may draft, but a human policy owner must approve meaning.
data.Rationale: Human accountability
data.Name: Human meaning approval
data.AttestationExposureNote: Unwatched and unowned: exposure defaults to the signatory.

data.Label: SMS consent required
data.Statement: SMS may be sent only to recipients with active consent.
data.Rationale: Consent and privacy
data.Name: SMS consent required
data.AttestationExposureNote: Unwatched and unowned: exposure defaults to the signatory.

data.Label: Quiet hours enforced
data.Statement: SMS delivery must not occur between 20:00 and 08:00 recipient-local time.
data.Rationale: Employee experience
data.Name: Quiet hours enforced
data.AttestationExposureNote: Unwatched and unowned: exposure defaults to the signatory.

data.Label: Opt-out text required
data.Statement: Every SMS must include approved opt-out language.
data.Rationale: Consent management
data.Name: Opt-out text required
data.AttestationExposureNote: Unwatched and unowned: exposure defaults to the signatory.

data.Label: Communication evidence retention
data.Statement: Rendered messages, approvals, recipient scope, and delivery results must be retained for 7 years.
data.Rationale: Auditability
data.Name: Communication evidence retention
data.AttestationExposureNote: Unwatched and unowned: exposure defaults to the signatory.

data.Label: Plain-language and accessibility
data.Statement: Email content must be readable, accessible, and include an alternate contact method.
data.Rationale: Inclusive communication
data.Name: Plain-language and accessibility
data.AttestationExposureNote: Unwatched and unowned: exposure defaults to the signatory.

data.Label: Zero energy before work
data.Statement: No maintenance starts until zero energy is verified at every isolation point.
data.Rationale: Hazardous energy control
data.Name: Zero energy before work
data.AttestationExposureNote: Owned but unwitnessed: rests on human judgement.

data.Label: One person, one lock
data.Statement: Every person working on the machine applies and removes their own lock.
data.Rationale: Hazardous energy control
data.Name: One person, one lock
data.AttestationExposureNote: Owned but unwitnessed: rests on human judgement.

data.Label: Recorded release approval
data.Statement: No production rollout without a recorded release approval.
data.Rationale: Change control
data.Name: Recorded release approval
data.AttestationExposureNote: Owned but unwitnessed: rests on human judgement.

KnowledgeFragments.Description: Explicit records of tacit, implicit, explicit, and situated procedural knowledge. This is an ERB-PKO extension represented as provenance-bearing dcat:Resource instances.

schema.name: KnowledgeFragmentId
schema.Description: Stored logical identifier for one KnowledgeFragments row.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Human-readable calculated display alias for the KnowledgeFragments row.

schema.name: ProcedureVersion
schema.Description: Procedure version informed by the fragment.

schema.name: Step
schema.Description: Optional step to which the fragment applies.

schema.name: KnowledgeForm
schema.Description: Tacit, Implicit, Explicit, SituatedJudgment, LessonLearned, or another declared form.

schema.name: Statement
schema.Description: Captured knowledge statement.

schema.name: ElicitationSession
schema.Description: Optional elicitation session that produced the fragment.

schema.name: SourceAgent
schema.Description: Practitioner or source agent.

schema.name: Confidence
schema.Description: Low, Medium, or High confidence.

schema.name: ValidFrom
schema.Description: Start of the fragment's valid-time interval.

schema.name: ValidTo
schema.Description: End of the fragment's valid-time interval.

schema.name: Status
schema.Description: Draft, Reviewed, Approved, Rejected, or Superseded.

schema.name: OwnerRole
schema.Description: Role accountable for maintaining the fragment.

schema.name: EvaluationContext
schema.Description: The evaluation context this row's time-dependent witnesses are judged under.

schema.name: AsOfInstant
schema.Description: The evaluation instant this row's time-dependent witnesses are judged against.

schema.name: IsCurrentlyValid
schema.Description: TRUE when the fragment is approved and valid now.

schema.name: SourceAgentIsStillEngaged
schema.Description: Whether the agent who is the source of this claim still holds a role here.

schema.name: SourceAgentKind
schema.Description: Whether the source of this claim is a Human, an AIAgent, or an AutomatedPipeline.

schema.name: HasHumanSource
schema.Description: TRUE when the claim originates from a human practitioner rather than software.

schema.name: HasOrphanedProvenance
schema.Description: TRUE when we still rely on this claim but the agent who gave it to us no longer holds a role here.

schema.name: IsUndefendableTacitClaim
schema.Description: TRUE when an orphaned claim is of a kind that lives in a person's head rather than in a document.

schema.name: IsApproved
schema.Description: TRUE when this claim has passed knowledge-authority approval.

schema.name: IsWithinValidityWindow
schema.Description: TRUE when this claim's stated validity window contains the present moment.

schema.name: IsReliedUpon
schema.Description: TRUE when this claim is attached to a specific step and is inside its validity window — i.e. it is operationally in play.

schema.name: StepProcedureVersionStatus
schema.Description: The procedure version owning the step this claim is attached to.

schema.name: IsAttachedToLiveVersion
schema.Description: Whether the procedure version this claim belongs to is currently executable.

schema.name: IsUnapprovedButReliedOn
schema.Description: TRUE when a live procedure is acting on a claim that has not been approved by the knowledge authority.

schema.name: EvidenceAgeDays
schema.Description: Age in days of the elicitation session this claim came from.

schema.name: HasRecordedElicitation
schema.Description: TRUE when this claim traces to a recorded elicitation session.

schema.name: IsFromSingleWitness
schema.Description: Whether this claim rests on a single practitioner's account.

schema.name: EvidenceExpiryDays
schema.Description: How many days this claim's evidence is trusted for, given how it was gathered.

schema.name: EvidenceHasExpired
schema.Description: TRUE when the evidence behind this claim is older than we trust evidence of its kind to be.

schema.name: OwnerAgent
schema.Description: The agent currently holding the role that owns this claim.

schema.name: IsAwaitingApproval
schema.Description: TRUE when this claim has been reviewed but not yet approved.

schema.name: OwnerIsMe
schema.Description: TRUE when the People Policy Owner role owns this claim.

schema.name: IsMyUnfinishedApproval
schema.Description: TRUE when a claim I own has been reviewed and is waiting on my approval.

schema.name: IsInvokedByAnException
schema.Description: How many documented exception handlers trigger on the same step this claim is attached to.

schema.name: HasOperationalReliance
schema.Description: TRUE when an exception handler exists on the step this claim governs.

schema.name: IsUnapprovedAndOperationallyLive
schema.Description: TRUE when a claim awaiting my approval is already being acted on through a documented exception path.

schema.name: AgeDays
schema.Description: Days since this claim became valid.

schema.name: IsLowConfidence
schema.Description: TRUE when this claim was recorded with less than high confidence.

schema.name: OwningVersionCadenceDays
schema.Description: The review cadence promised for the version this claim supports.

schema.name: ExceedsOwningCadence
schema.Description: TRUE when this claim is older than the review cadence promised for the version it supports.

schema.name: IsAgingLowConfidenceClaim
schema.Description: TRUE when a claim we were never sure about has also outlived its version's review cadence.

schema.name: OwnerRoleAgentKind
schema.Description: Agent kind of whoever currently holds the role that owns this knowledge fragment.

schema.name: IsHumanOwned
schema.Description: TRUE when the owning role is currently held by a human.

schema.name: IsAiValidatedByAi
schema.Description: TRUE when knowledge came from a non-human source AND is owned by a non-human-held role.

schema.name: ReviewCadenceDays
schema.Description: The review cadence promised for the procedure version this fragment supports, resolved via ProcedureVersions because INDEX/MATCH only matches a target primary key.

schema.name: IsOverdueForReview
schema.Description: TRUE when a currently-valid fragment has gone longer than its stewardship cadence without review.

schema.name: PredatesCurrentRoleHolder
schema.Description: TRUE when this knowledge became valid before the current holder of its owning role took the role.

schema.name: OwnerRoleAssignmentValidFrom
schema.Description: When the current holder of the owning role took that role.

schema.name: LastReviewedAt
schema.Description: When this fragment was last actually reviewed and reaffirmed by its owning role. Null when it has never been reviewed since authoring. IsOverdueForReview infers recency from ValidFrom, which records when the claim became TRUE, not when anyone last looked at it. Those are different events, and the inference is deliberately left in place under its own name rather than silently rewritten to fall back on this column.

schema.name: FragilitySignalCount
schema.Description: How many of the four loop-1 decay signals are simultaneously true for this fragment: single witness, overdue for review, low confidence, operational reliance.

schema.name: IsCompoundFragile
schema.Description: A fragment carrying at least three of the four decay signals at once.

schema.name: IsSinglePointOfFailure
schema.Description: A claim that rests on exactly one person's word and that an active exception handler actually routes cases against.

schema.name: IsExpiringSinglePointOfFailure
schema.Description: A single-sourced, operationally relied-upon claim that is also past its review date.

schema.name: CompoundFragileVersionKey
schema.Description: Composite-key echo: this fragment's procedure version when the fragment is compound-fragile, blank otherwise.

schema.name: ValidFragmentSessionKey
schema.Description: Composite-key echo: the elicitation session behind this fragment when the fragment is currently valid, blank otherwise.

schema.name: ConsumingStepIsSoftwareAssigned
schema.Description: Whether the step that consumes this fragment is assigned to an AI agent or an automated pipeline.

schema.name: ConsumingStepAgentKind
schema.Description: The kind of agent currently holding the role assigned to the step that consumes this fragment.

schema.name: IsUnapprovedAndMachineConsumed
schema.Description: An unapproved claim that a software-assigned step actually relies on — executed literally, with no human in position to notice it is wrong.

schema.name: IsUnapprovedAndHumanConsumed
schema.Description: An unapproved claim relied on by a human-assigned step — a reviewable risk rather than a silent one.

schema.name: MachineConsumedUnapprovedVersionKey
schema.Description: Composite-key echo: this fragment's procedure version when the fragment is unapproved and machine-consumed, blank otherwise.

schema.name: HasReviewRecord
schema.Description: Whether this fragment has ever had an actual review recorded, as opposed to merely having a ValidFrom date.

schema.name: DaysSinceActualReview
schema.Description: Days elapsed since this fragment was last actually reviewed. Zero when no review has ever been recorded — read this only alongside HasReviewRecord, never on its own.

schema.name: IsUnreviewedSinceAuthoring
schema.Description: A currently-valid claim that nobody has ever reviewed since it was written.

schema.name: IsGenuinelyOverdue
schema.Description: A valid claim whose LAST ACTUAL REVIEW is older than the cadence its owning version promised.

schema.name: ReviewRecencyIsInferred
schema.Description: A fragment reported overdue by the loop-1 inference purely because no review has ever been recorded — the number is an artifact of missing data, not evidence of neglect.

schema.name: InferenceDisagreesWithRecord
schema.Description: A fragment the ValidFrom inference calls overdue but which was in fact reviewed inside its cadence — a false positive in the loop-1 predicate, now provable.

schema.name: GenuinelyOverdueVersionKey
schema.Description: Composite-key echo: this fragment's procedure version when the fragment is genuinely overdue, blank otherwise.

schema.name: RatifiedBoundaryCount
schema.Description: How many currently-binding authority boundaries this fragment ratifies.

schema.name: RelianceSurfaceCount
schema.Description: Total number of distinct downstream dependents on this claim: exception handlers plus ratified authority boundaries.

schema.name: DaysAwaitingMyApproval
schema.Description: How long a claim of mine has been sitting at Reviewed without my approval. Zero when the claim is not mine or is already decided.

schema.name: IsHighBlastRadiusUnapproved
schema.Description: An unapproved, operationally live claim of mine with more than one distinct downstream dependent.

schema.name: IsLongUnapproved
schema.Description: A claim that has waited on my signature for more than thirty days.

schema.name: UnapprovedLoadBearingVersionKey
schema.Description: Composite-key echo: this fragment's procedure version when it is a high-blast-radius unapproved claim, blank otherwise.

schema.name: OwnerRoleIsVacated
schema.Description: Whether the role that owns this claim is currently vacated.

schema.name: IsOrphanedByRole
schema.Description: A currently-valid claim whose owning role nobody holds — accountable to a vacancy.

schema.name: ValidFragmentVersionKey
schema.Description: Composite-key echo: this fragment's owning procedure version when the fragment is currently valid, blank otherwise.

schema.name: SemanticTypeIri
schema.Description: Extension class IRI.

schema.name: CognitiveBasis
schema.Description: Intuition, PatternRecognition or Judgment for tacit knowledge; Articulated for knowledge stated outright.

schema.name: TacitnessDegree
schema.Description: Position on the tacit-to-explicit spectrum: 1 fully articulated to 5 not articulable.

schema.name: LostInTranslation
schema.Description: What the explicit statement fails to carry of the practice it was drawn from.

schema.name: EncodedAs
schema.Description: HardRule, ConditionedGuidance, CueNarrative or Statement.

schema.name: StatedConditions
schema.Description: The conditions under which the fragment holds, as captured.

schema.name: IsFlattenedToBrittleRule
schema.Description: TRUE when tacit or situated knowledge was encoded as a hard rule with no conditions saying when it holds.

schema.name: CorroborationCount
schema.Description: Independent supporting data points.

schema.name: RestsOnSingleDataPoint
schema.Description: TRUE for approved knowledge no second session or practitioner supports.

schema.name: OwnerOrganization
schema.Description: The organization that owns the procedure this row belongs to, one hop at a time from Procedures.OwnerOrganization. A row policy compares it to the caller's organization, so a plant sign-in never sees the finance close.

KnowledgeGaps.Description: Known unknowns and missing procedural coverage. Explicit ERB-PKO extension used to govern scope and prevent silent incompleteness.

schema.name: KnowledgeGapId
schema.Description: Stored logical identifier for one KnowledgeGaps row.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Human-readable calculated display alias for the KnowledgeGaps row.

schema.name: ProcedureVersion
schema.Description: Affected procedure version.

schema.name: Step
schema.Description: Affected step.

schema.name: Statement
schema.Description: What is not yet known or represented.

schema.name: Severity
schema.Description: Low, Medium, High, or Critical.

schema.name: BlockingKind
schema.Description: Blocking or NonBlocking.

schema.name: Status
schema.Description: Open, Investigating, Resolved, AcceptedRisk, or Closed.

schema.name: OwnerRole
schema.Description: Role responsible for resolving the gap.

schema.name: IdentifiedAt
schema.Description: Time the gap was identified.

schema.name: ResolutionPlan
schema.Description: Resolution plan or final resolution.

schema.name: IsOpen
schema.Description: TRUE when the gap remains open.

schema.name: OpenGapVersionKey
schema.Description: Echoes the ProcedureVersion id for open high-severity knowledge gaps.

schema.name: IsBlocking
schema.Description: TRUE when this gap is declared blocking rather than informational.

schema.name: IsOpenAndBlocking
schema.Description: TRUE when this gap is both unresolved and declared blocking.

schema.name: EvaluationContext
schema.Description: The evaluation context this row's time-dependent witnesses are judged under.

schema.name: AsOfInstant
schema.Description: The evaluation instant this row's time-dependent witnesses are judged against.

schema.name: DaysOpen
schema.Description: Days this gap has been unresolved, or zero once closed.

schema.name: ToleranceDays
schema.Description: How long a gap of this severity may remain open before it becomes a governance failure in its own right.

schema.name: IsOverdueGap
schema.Description: TRUE when this acknowledged unknown has outlived the tolerance for its severity.

schema.name: OwnerAgent
schema.Description: The agent currently holding the role that owns resolving this gap.

schema.name: OwnerIsStillEngaged
schema.Description: Whether the agent responsible for closing this gap still holds a role here.

schema.name: HasResolutionPlan
schema.Description: TRUE when someone has written down how this gap would be closed.

schema.name: IsAbandonedUnknown
schema.Description: TRUE when an overdue gap has either no plan or no living owner — an admission of ignorance that nobody is acting on.

schema.name: OpenBlockingGapVersionKey
schema.Description: Composite-key echo: this gap's procedure version when the gap is both open and blocking, blank otherwise.

schema.name: OwnerRoleIsVacated
schema.Description: Whether the role that owns this gap is currently vacated.

schema.name: IsOwnerlessOpenGap
schema.Description: An open gap whose owning role nobody currently holds — an acknowledged unknown with nobody accountable for closing it.

schema.name: SemanticTypeIri
schema.Description: Extension class IRI.

schema.name: GapCause
schema.Description: Gatekeeping, Sabotage, Undocumented or Unknown; blank when never classified.

schema.name: HolderDeclinedToShare
schema.Description: TRUE when an elicitation recorded the one person who knows declining to share it.

schema.name: SiloedWithin
schema.Description: The group the knowledge stays inside.

schema.name: DrawnOutBySession
schema.Description: The session that drew the gatekept knowledge out.

schema.name: CodifiedAsFragment
schema.Description: The fragment it was codified as.

schema.name: IsKnownAndUnresolved
schema.Description: TRUE for an identified gap that is still open.

schema.name: IsGatekeepingOrSabotage
schema.Description: TRUE for a gap caused by gatekeeping or knowledge sabotage.

schema.name: IsUnattributedGatekeeping
schema.Description: TRUE when a holder was recorded declining to share but the gap is not identified as gatekeeping or sabotage.

data.Statement: req-close-separation stated the preparer may not be the final approver, but nothing evaluated it. The control existed only as prose in a Requirements row, so a violation would have been invisible.
data.ResolutionPlan: Resolved by StepExecutions.ViolatesSeparationOfDuties, which counts preparation steps in the same procedure execution performed by the agent now approving. Verified by staging a breach (maria-chen approving se-close05 after preparing se-close03): the witness read TRUE. The staged breach was reverted; the control now reads FALSE because separation genuinely holds, not because nothing is checking.
data.Name: High: req-close-separation stated the preparer may not be the fina

data.Statement: StewardshipAssignments promised a 90-day review cadence for close-v1.1.0 and 60 days for policy-v1.0.0. Both the promise and the actual review history were in the model and nothing compared them, so a lapsed cadence was invisible.
data.ResolutionPlan: Resolved by ReviewEvents.ExceedsPromisedCadence and PromiseAndBehaviorDisagree, which compare DaysSinceReviewed against the cadence promised by the version's stewardship assignment. Surfacing the real Q1 review (review-close-q1) showed the witness firing on genuine history: 121 days elapsed against a 90-day promise. The Q2 review closed the lapse, so current state reads compliant.
data.Name: Medium: StewardshipAssignments promised a 90-day review cadence for

data.Statement: Five of twelve roles were held only by a denormalized Roles.CurrentAgent pointer with no RoleAssignments row: communications-manager, knowledge-authority, process-steward, close-automation, policy-drafting-agent. The convenience pointer claimed a holder the auditable time-bounded table could not confirm, so provenance for anything those roles touched was unverifiable.
data.ResolutionPlan: Surfaced by Agents.IsStillEngaged, which counts CURRENT RoleAssignments rather than trusting Roles.CurrentAgent. amina-yusuf read as not engaged, which made kf-policy-channel an IsUndefendableTacitClaim. Resolved by recording the five missing time-bounded assignments. The witness stays: it is the only thing that distinguishes a real appointment from a denormalized pointer.
data.Name: High: Five of twelve roles were held only by a denormalized Roles.

data.Statement: comm-sms-policy set ConsentRequired=true and exc-no-sms-consent documented the suppress-and-email handling, but no per-recipient delivery record existed, so a send to a non-consenting recipient was structurally invisible. req-policy-consent was a blocking control with zero satisfaction records.
data.ResolutionPlan: Resolved by the Recipients and MessageDeliveries tables plus MessageDeliveries.IsConsentViolation. Proven on md-003, a real SMS to a never-consented recipient, which the witness flags while correctly NOT flagging md-004 (consent revoked, properly suppressed under exc-no-sms-consent) or md-006 (unreachable, failed, HR case opened). Recipient re-consented; the delivery row is retained as evidence.
data.Name: Critical: comm-sms-policy set ConsentRequired=true and exc-no-sms-cons

data.Statement: comm-sms-policy defined a 20:00-08:00 quiet window and nothing compared a send time against it.
data.ResolutionPlan: Resolved by MessageDeliveries.IsInsideQuietWindow and IsQuietHoursViolation, proven on md-005 (21:00 send). QuietHoursStartHour is stored rather than parsed: VALUE(LEFT("20:00",2)) does not translate — the transpiler casts the string to a timestamp and the view errors.
data.Name: High: comm-sms-policy defined a 20:00-08:00 quiet window and nothi

data.Statement: MessageTemplates carried Status="Approved" as a bare string with no approval record behind it, and nothing evaluated a send BEFORE transmission. Every gate the communication policies define — consent, quiet hours, length, opt-out, approval — was checkable only after the fact, if at all.
data.ResolutionPlan: Resolved by the SendIntents table and IsClearedToSend, which gates a proposed send on permission, timing, content, and authorization before it happens, and names the blocking gate. Proven across seven intents: Timing blocks a 21:00 send, Content blocks an oversized body and one missing the STOP phrase, Permission blocks an unreachable recipient. Authorization blocked ALL sends until tmpl-policy-sms received a real approval record (tap-sms-001) — the pipeline had been transmitting under a template nobody had attributably approved.
data.Name: Critical: MessageTemplates carried Status="Approved" as a bare string

ChangeRequests.Description: Governed requests for semantic or operational change, anchored to a procedure version and authority. Explicit ERB-PKO extension.

schema.name: ChangeRequestId
schema.Description: Stored logical identifier for one ChangeRequests row.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Human-readable calculated display alias for the ChangeRequests row.

schema.name: ProcedureVersion
schema.Description: Procedure version affected.

schema.name: Title
schema.Description: Change title.

schema.name: ChangeKind
schema.Description: Defect, Enhancement, NewRequirement, DataOperation, or BreakingChange.

schema.name: Status
schema.Description: Draft, UnderReview, Approved, Rejected, Implemented, or Closed.

schema.name: RequestedByAgent
schema.Description: Agent requesting the change.

schema.name: AuthorityRole
schema.Description: Role authorized to approve the change.

schema.name: RequestedAt
schema.Description: Request time.

schema.name: DecidedAt
schema.Description: Decision time.

schema.name: ImpactAssessment
schema.Description: Expected effect on commitments, data, projections, and tests.

schema.name: IsOpen
schema.Description: TRUE while the change request is still outstanding. An Approved request stays open until ImplementedAt records that it actually landed — approval is a decision, not an outcome.

schema.name: OpenChangeVersionKey
schema.Description: Echoes the ProcedureVersion id only for change requests still open.

schema.name: IsDecided
schema.Description: TRUE when a decision timestamp has been recorded.

schema.name: EvaluationContext
schema.Description: The evaluation context this row's time-dependent witnesses are judged under.

schema.name: AsOfInstant
schema.Description: The evaluation instant this row's time-dependent witnesses are judged against.

schema.name: DaysPending
schema.Description: Days from request to decision, or to now if still undecided.

schema.name: IsStillPending
schema.Description: TRUE when the request is in an open status and has no decision recorded.

schema.name: IsStalled
schema.Description: TRUE when an undecided change request has been pending more than fourteen days.

schema.name: AuthorityAgent
schema.Description: The agent currently holding the authority role that owes a decision on this request.

schema.name: RequesterIsAuthority
schema.Description: TRUE when the agent who raised the request is also the agent who decides it.

schema.name: AwaitsAuthorityDecision
schema.Description: TRUE when this request is formally before its authority and no decision has been recorded.

schema.name: AuthorityRoleLabel
schema.Description: Human-readable label of the role that owes a decision.

schema.name: TouchesLiveVersion
schema.Description: Whether the version this request would alter is currently executable.

schema.name: IsLiveDecisionBacklog
schema.Description: TRUE when a decision I owe is blocking a change to a procedure currently in production.

schema.name: BlocksAnOpenGap
schema.Description: TRUE when an undecided request against a live version is the kind that exists to close a known gap.

schema.name: ImplementedAt
schema.Description: When the approved change was actually applied to the procedure version. Null until it lands. Distinct from DecidedAt, which records only that the authority ruled. Approval and implementation are separate events; conflating them is what left IsOpen with no terminal state.

schema.name: BacklogVersionKey
schema.Description: Composite-key echo: this request's procedure version when it is live decision backlog, blank otherwise.

schema.name: IsMyPendingDecision
schema.Description: A change request awaiting a decision that is mine personally to make.

schema.name: IsMyBlockingBacklog
schema.Description: A decision waiting on me that is holding an open gap on a live procedure.

schema.name: IsMyOverdueBacklog
schema.Description: A blocking decision that has waited on me for more than two weeks.

schema.name: IsImplemented
schema.Description: Whether the approved change has actually been applied.

schema.name: IsMyDecidedRequest
schema.Description: A change request I have personally ruled on.

schema.name: IsMyDecidedButUnlanded
schema.Description: A decision I have made that has not yet been applied — still counted against me by the loop-1 open-request measure.

schema.name: DecisionLatencyDays
schema.Description: How many days I took to rule, once ruled. Zero when undecided — read only alongside IsDecided.

schema.name: ImplementationLatencyDays
schema.Description: How many days elapsed between my ruling and the change actually landing. Zero when not yet implemented.

schema.name: DelayIsDownstreamOfMe
schema.Description: A request I decided promptly that is nevertheless still outstanding because nobody has implemented it.

schema.name: UnlandedVersionKey
schema.Description: Composite-key echo: this request's procedure version when I have decided it but it has not landed, blank otherwise.

schema.name: IsApprovedNotImplemented
schema.Description: A change request the authority approved but that has not yet been applied.

schema.name: DaysSinceApproval
schema.Description: How many days have elapsed since the authority decided this request. Zero when undecided.

schema.name: IsStalledImplementation
schema.Description: An approved change request that has sat unimplemented for more than two weeks.

schema.name: StalledImplementationVersionKey
schema.Description: Composite-key echo: this request's procedure version when its implementation is stalled, blank otherwise.

schema.name: ApprovedVersionKey
schema.Description: Echoes the target version id when this change request was approved.

schema.name: IsApprovedDecision
schema.Description: TRUE when this change request was decided in the affirmative.

schema.name: SemanticTypeIri
schema.Description: Extension class IRI.

schema.name: OwnerOrganization
schema.Description: The organization that owns the procedure this row belongs to, one hop at a time from Procedures.OwnerOrganization. A row policy compares it to the caller's organization, so a plant sign-in never sees the finance close.

schema.name: ProcedureVersion
schema.Description: Reviewed procedure version.

schema.name: ReviewKind
schema.Description: Review type.

schema.name: ReviewedAt
schema.Description: Review timestamp.

schema.name: ReviewedByAgent
schema.Description: Reviewing agent.

schema.name: Outcome
schema.Description: Passed, PassedWithChange, Failed, or Deferred.

schema.name: RelatedChangeRequest
schema.Description: Change request produced or considered.

schema.name: NextReviewDue
schema.Description: Next required review.

schema.name: EvaluationContext
schema.Description: The evaluation context this row's time-dependent witnesses are judged under.

schema.name: AsOfInstant
schema.Description: The evaluation instant this row's time-dependent witnesses are judged against.

schema.name: IsOverdue
schema.Description: TRUE when review is overdue.

schema.name: OverdueVersionKey
schema.Description: Echoes the ProcedureVersion id only when this review is past its next-due date.

schema.name: PromisedCadenceDays
schema.Description: The review cadence promised for this procedure version, resolved via ProcedureVersions because INDEX/MATCH can only match a target table primary key.

schema.name: DaysSinceReviewed

schema.name: ExceedsPromisedCadence
schema.Description: TRUE when more days have elapsed since this review than the stewardship assignment promised as a cadence.

schema.name: CadenceDriftDays

schema.name: PromiseAndBehaviorDisagree

schema.name: CadenceBreachVersionKey
schema.Description: Composite-key echo: this review event's procedure version when the promised cadence has been exceeded, blank otherwise.

schema.name: SemanticTypeIri
schema.Description: Class IRI used in projection.

schema.name: VersionModifiedAt

schema.name: ReviewDidNotRefreshModified

schema.name: OperationalBindingId
schema.Description: Stored logical identifier for one OperationalBindings row.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Human-readable calculated display alias for the OperationalBindings row.

schema.name: ProcedureVersion
schema.Description: Procedure version using the binding.

schema.name: Step
schema.Description: Step using the binding.

schema.name: Resource
schema.Description: Bound operational resource.

schema.name: AccessMode
schema.Description: Read, Write, ReadWrite, Subscribe, or Publish.

schema.name: RecordOrSchemaKey
schema.Description: Operational record, table, event, or schema key.

schema.name: LastObservedAt
schema.Description: Most recent successful observation.

schema.name: FreshnessSlaMinutes
schema.Description: Maximum allowed data age.

schema.name: IsAuthoritative
schema.Description: TRUE when the binding is authoritative for the represented fact.

schema.name: EvaluationContext
schema.Description: The evaluation context this row's time-dependent witnesses are judged under.

schema.name: AsOfInstant
schema.Description: The evaluation instant this row's time-dependent witnesses are judged against.

schema.name: AgeMinutes
schema.Description: Current observed age.

schema.name: IsFresh
schema.Description: TRUE when within freshness SLA.

schema.name: StaleBindingStepKey
schema.Description: Echoes the bound Step id only when the binding is outside its freshness SLA.

schema.name: AuthoritativeStaleStepKey
schema.Description: Echoes the bound Step id only when an AUTHORITATIVE binding is stale.

schema.name: IsStaleAndAuthoritative
schema.Description: TRUE when an authoritative binding has aged past its freshness SLA.

schema.name: StepWhenStale
schema.Description: Echoes the step id when this authoritative binding is stale, blank otherwise.

schema.name: ResourceIsApproved

schema.name: IsUsableForDrafting
schema.Description: TRUE when this binding points at an approved source that is still inside its freshness SLA.

schema.name: StepWhenUnusable
schema.Description: Echoes the step id when this binding is NOT usable for drafting, blank otherwise.

schema.name: SemanticTypeIri
schema.Description: Extension class IRI.

CommunicationPolicies.Description: Channel-specific communication policy projected from the same canonical procedure. Uses ODRL-style policy semantics plus ERB-PKO channel constraints.

schema.name: CommunicationPolicyId
schema.Description: Stored logical identifier for one CommunicationPolicies row.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Human-readable calculated display alias for the CommunicationPolicies row.

schema.name: ProcedureVersion
schema.Description: Procedure version governing the channel.

schema.name: Channel
schema.Description: Email, SMS, Push, Postal, or another declared channel.

schema.name: AudienceRule
schema.Description: Rule that identifies eligible recipients.

schema.name: ConsentRequired
schema.Description: Whether active consent is required.

schema.name: QuietHoursStart
schema.Description: Recipient-local quiet-hours start.

schema.name: QuietHoursEnd
schema.Description: Recipient-local quiet-hours end.

schema.name: MaxMessageLength
schema.Description: Maximum message length for one unit.

schema.name: MaxSegments
schema.Description: Maximum number of channel segments.

schema.name: RetentionDays
schema.Description: Retention period for rendered messages and delivery records.

schema.name: ApprovalRole
schema.Description: Role approving the channel policy.

schema.name: RequiredContent
schema.Description: Content that every message must include.

schema.name: AuthorityStatement
schema.Description: Which artifact is authoritative.

schema.name: Status
schema.Description: Draft, Active, Suspended, or Retired.

schema.name: ConsentViolationCount
schema.Description: Number of consent violations attributable to this channel policy.

schema.name: QuietHoursStartHour
schema.Description: The hour (0-23) at which the quiet window opens. Stored rather than parsed from QuietHoursStart: VALUE(LEFT(...)) does not translate — the transpiler casts the "20:00" string to a timestamp and the view errors. The sending system already knows this number, so modeling it as a parse would dress a broken derivation up as a rule.

schema.name: QuietHoursEndHour
schema.Description: Numeric hour 0-23 at which quiet hours end. Seeded 8 for comm-sms-policy, 0 for comm-email-policy.

schema.name: QuietHoursViolationCount
schema.Description: Number of transmitted messages that breached this policy's quiet-hours window.

schema.name: RequiredOptOutPhrase
schema.Description: The exact opt-out phrase every message on this channel must contain. Seeded 'Reply STOP' for comm-sms-policy, empty string for comm-email-policy.

schema.name: IsActivePolicy
schema.Description: TRUE only when this channel policy is in Active status.

schema.name: SemanticTypeIri
schema.Description: ODRL Policy class IRI.

MessageTemplates.Description: Approved channel templates projected from the canonical rulebook without becoming a second source of policy meaning.

schema.name: MessageTemplateId
schema.Description: Stored logical identifier for one MessageTemplates row.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Human-readable calculated display alias for the MessageTemplates row.

schema.name: CommunicationPolicy
schema.Description: Channel policy governing the template.

schema.name: Resource
schema.Description: Template resource.

schema.name: SubjectTemplate
schema.Description: Subject template where supported.

schema.name: BodyTemplate
schema.Description: Body template.

schema.name: Locale
schema.Description: Locale or language tag.

schema.name: Status
schema.Description: Draft, Approved, Retired, or Superseded.

schema.name: PolicyMaxMessageLength
schema.Description: Per-segment character limit inherited from the governing channel policy.

schema.name: PolicyMaxSegments
schema.Description: Maximum permitted segment count from the governing channel policy.

schema.name: BodyTemplateLength
schema.Description: Character length of the raw template body before variable substitution.

schema.name: IsTemplateOverLength
schema.Description: TRUE when the template body alone already exceeds the single-segment limit before any variables are substituted in.

schema.name: ValidApprovalCount
schema.Description: Number of properly-authorized approvals on record for this template.

schema.name: HasValidApproval
schema.Description: TRUE when at least one properly-authorized approval exists for this template.

schema.name: IsClaimingUnbackedApproval
schema.Description: TRUE when a template's Status says Approved but no properly-authorized approval record backs it. The phantom-approval witness.

schema.name: CurrentBodyHash
schema.Description: Digest of the template's current body text, maintained whenever the body is edited.

schema.name: LastApprovedBodyHash
schema.Description: Digest of the body text as it stood at the most recent valid approval.

schema.name: LastValidApproval
schema.Description: The TemplateApprovals id of the approval this template is currently sendable under. Deliberately a raw identifier, not a relationship: TemplateApprovals already points at MessageTemplates, so declaring an FK back would make the two tables mutually dependent and the rulebook is required to stay acyclic. The value is still resolved by INDEX/MATCH in LastApprovedBodyHash.

schema.name: HasBodyDrifted
schema.Description: TRUE when the template body no longer matches what was approved.

schema.name: IsSendableUnderApproval
schema.Description: TRUE only when the template is marked Approved, has a properly-authorized approval, AND its body still matches what was approved.

schema.name: DriftedSendCount
schema.Description: How many messages went out from this template while it was not validly sendable.

schema.name: UnansweredDeliveryCount
schema.Description: How many transmitted messages from this template drew no acknowledgement.

schema.name: TransmittedDeliveryCount
schema.Description: How many deliveries using this template were actually transmitted.

schema.name: TemplateDrawsNoResponse
schema.Description: TRUE when every transmitted message from this template went unacknowledged.

schema.name: LastApprovalAt
schema.Description: When this template's currently-governing approval was decided.

schema.name: SemanticTypeIri
schema.Description: Resource class IRI.

WitnessLoops.Description: One row per role-question expansion loop. Each loop poses questions that only became askable because of the previous loop's predicates.

schema.name: WitnessLoopId
schema.Description: Stored logical identifier for one WitnessLoops row.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Human-readable calculated display alias for the WitnessLoops row.

schema.name: LoopNumber
schema.Description: Ordinal of this expansion loop. Loop 1 is the founding set of role questions.

schema.name: Title
schema.Description: Short title for what this loop set out to make askable.

schema.name: Premise
schema.Description: Why this loop's questions became askable. For loop N>1 this names the loop N-1 predicates that made them possible.

schema.name: StartedAt
schema.Description: Time this loop began.

schema.name: CompletedAt
schema.Description: Time this loop was committed. Null while in progress.

schema.name: QuestionCount
schema.Description: How many role questions were posed in this loop.

schema.name: IsComplete
schema.Description: TRUE once the loop has been committed.

schema.name: FieldsAfter
schema.Description: Total fields in the rulebook after this loop completed.

schema.name: DerivedAfter
schema.Description: Derived fields after this loop completed.

schema.name: WitnessedAfter
schema.Description: Fields invented for a role question after this loop completed.

data.Title: The founding questions
data.Premise: The model specified obligations precisely and witnessed their breach almost nowhere. Requirements, verifications, exceptions, and communication policies were all stated with real precision, and in each case the execution-side counterpart that would catch a violation was missing. Loop 1 asks each of the twelve named roles what it actually needs to know, and invents the atomic predicates required to answer.
data.Name: Loop 1: The founding questions

data.Title: Questions only loop 1 made askable
data.Premise: Loop 1 established WHAT can go wrong: a blocking control unmet, a verification skipped, a send refused, a claim whose source has left. Loop 2 asks the questions that only exist once those columns do — about the QUALITY of the assurance rather than its presence. Three examples that had no expressible form before loop 1 ran: only 4 of 13 requirements have any computed witness at all, so which controls are still trusted purely on assertion; verification_outcomes.is_self_witnessed reads 3/4, so how much of the evidence is the executor vouching for themselves; and send_intents.is_silently_dropped reads 4/7, a failure mode that could not be named until IsClearedToSend existed to refuse a send in the first place. Every loop-2 question records, in its own provenance, the loop-1 predicates that made it possible.
data.Name: Loop 2: Questions only loop 1 made askable

data.Title: Loop 3: the three gaps the source articles named and the model didn't have
data.Premise: Comparing this rulebook against the four "Intentional Arrangement" Process Knowledge Management articles surfaced three concepts the essays argue for at length that had no table: process mining as an elicitation channel, controlled vocabulary/taxonomy, and the informal knowledge-broker network. Unlike loops 1-2, this loop is not a full 12-role sweep — it is exactly these three named gaps, each owned by the role that would actually ask the question.
data.Name: Loop 3: Loop 3: the three gaps the source articles named and the model didn't have

data.Title: Structure the executions cannot show
data.Premise: Every witness in loops 1-3 reads either a single row or a single edge: whether this transition was traversed, whether this control was satisfied. The step graph itself is cyclic (Fallback and Alternative transitions send work back to earlier steps), and questions about its shape (which steps can be re-entered, which controls must hold on every pass) are reachability over paths of any length. Transitive closure is provably not expressible in first-order logic with aggregates, so no formula answers them. Loop 4 adds the closure of StepTransitions as a substrate-native closure field and asks the questions only it makes askable.
data.Name: Loop 4: Structure the executions cannot show

data.Title: Loop 6: the full PKO class model, lockout/tagout, and a governed deployment
data.Premise: Loop 5 put every claim of the five source articles into the rulebook and computed what the model covers. The largest block of uncovered claims was structural: PKO 2.0.0 classes and properties with no table (multi-steps and their children, input and output variables, the entities an execution used and generated, status-change kinds, FAQ categories and targets, the industry module's machines, energy sources, locks and protective equipment), and the two worked procedures the articles tell their story through. This loop adds both, and every new predicate is asked for by the technician, safety officer, steward or knowledge engineer doing that work.
data.Name: Loop 6: Loop 6: the full PKO class model, lockout/tagout, and a governed deployment

data.Title: Loop 8: organizing collected knowledge before modeling it
data.Premise: Loop 6 gave the model the full PKO class model and two worked procedures; loop 7 records how their knowledge was collected. Nothing yet says how that material is organized: at which level of abstraction a statement lives, which stakeholder lens a view serves, where a piece of knowledge applies and where it stops, how coarse a step is, which taxonomy branch a procedure sits in, which wording practitioners use for an activity or a role, and whether the controlled terms still mean what the organization means. This loop organizes it, and every predicate is asked for by the steward, knowledge engineer, auditor, product manager, infrastructure engineer, operations manager or executive who needs that organization to do their work.
data.Name: Loop 8: Loop 8: organizing collected knowledge before modeling it

data.Title: Loop 9: encoded knowledge in use -- retrieval, AI grounding, projections and feedback
data.Premise: Loop 6 gave the model the lockout/tagout and production-deployment procedures, their executions and the AI risk classifier. Nothing yet recorded how that knowledge leaves the rulebook: which systems hold which version, what graph an AI assistant was served and whether a reasoner checked it, which segments and assertions grounded an answer, what prompts carried, which documents were generated from the model, what practitioners annotated, searched for and failed to find, and what outcomes followed. Those records only became judgeable once loop 6 made the steps, transitions, conditions, cues and requirements explicit enough to check an AI's output against. Every predicate here is asked for by the knowledge engineer, steward, safety officer, release manager, AI enablement lead or the plant assistant itself.
data.Name: Loop 9: Loop 9: encoded knowledge in use -- retrieval, AI grounding, projections and feedback

data.Title: Loop 10: the model governs itself: ownership, versioning, change control and question review
data.Premise: Loops 6 to 9 gave the procedures their full structure, organization and encoding, and every one of those loops changed this rulebook's schema. Nothing recorded who was allowed to make those changes, which competency question motivated them, what their impact assessment found, which semantic version they shipped in, or whether the original questions still answer afterwards. This loop makes the model's own governance data: named steward and authority charters, a change log and change requests with impact findings and validation runs, releases whose version numbers are checked against their contents, drift observations, and a competency-question baseline re-run per release.
data.Name: Loop 10: Loop 10: the model governs itself: ownership, versioning, change control and question review

data.Title: Loop 11: sourcing, knowledge audit, the AI system registry and ground-truth routing
data.Premise: Loop 6 gave the model a governed production deployment with an AI risk classifier, role assignments with validity periods, and the artifacts each step produces and consumes. What the model still could not say was where the organization's process knowledge actually lives once execution is sent to providers, what an audit of held against needed knowledge finds, whether provider relationships move knowledge back, which AI systems the registry knows that the graph does not, what an agent upgrade touches, and whether the assignments that a deployment pipeline routes approval notices from were updated before the run that needed them. This loop adds each of those, with seeded breaches on the deployment scenario.
data.Name: Loop 11: Loop 11: sourcing, knowledge audit, the AI system registry and ground-truth routing

data.Title: Loop 7: elicitation methods and tacit knowledge
data.Premise: Loop 6 gave the model a lockout/tagout procedure encoded from veterans' workshops, with the executions that show where practice departs from the SOP. What the model still could not say was how that knowledge was drawn out: which methods were combined, whether interviews asked why and what happens when the procedure falls short, what observation saw that the practitioner never mentioned, who was in the workshop, which disagreements were settled, what an expert knows but cannot say, where the knowledge lived before and after, and whether gatekept knowledge was ever drawn out. This loop adds each of those with seeded breaches.
data.Name: Loop 7: Loop 7: elicitation methods and tacit knowledge

data.Title: Loop 12: the social side of collection: holders, brokers, communities, trust and turnover
data.Premise: Loops 6 to 11 gave the model procedures, executions, role assignments with departures, a broker network, communities of practice and a sourcing audit. What the model still could not say was who carries each piece of know-how (a person, a facility or a system), how it travels, who bridges communities and translates their vocabularies, what a source withholds under which power dynamic, whether departments disagree about the same process, whether mentors have time and sharers are rewarded, and whether knowledge and solved problems survive staff turnover. This loop adds each of those, with seeded breaches on the lockout and deployment scenarios.
data.Name: Loop 12: Loop 12: the social side of collection: holders, brokers, communities, trust and turnover

data.Title: Loop 13: provenance, traceability, process mining and the document-practice gap
data.Premise: Earlier loops recorded collected source material, elicitation sessions, knowledge fragments with a source agent, and process-mining runs as variant counts. What the model could not say was which collected material each process model, step and constraint came from and in what role, whether that source has changed since, who derived and who confirmed each item, where the mined flow departs from the documented one and where it waits, whether documents trail practice, and whether failures, feedback and recurring reviews actually flow back into collection. This loop adds each of those, with seeded breaches on the deployment and lockout scenarios.
data.Name: Loop 13: Loop 13: provenance, traceability, process mining and the document-practice gap

data.Title: Loop 14: use cases, experts, pilots and real data behind each governed model
data.Premise: Loops 6 to 13 left a handful of article claims uncovered. Four are practices the Linked Open Terms methodology prescribes and theme E's governed models could not witness: starting from a real use case, domain experts in every activity, refinement through pilots, and implementation over real data.
data.Name: Loop 14: Loop 14: use cases, experts, pilots and real data behind each governed model

data.Title: The machinery around the knowledge: encoding technologies, funding programmes, published terms
data.Premise: Loops 6 to 14 modelled ACME's procedural knowledge itself. Five article claims had no honest witness afterwards, because each is about the machinery around that knowledge rather than the knowledge: whether the systems holding it can query, validate and reason over it; whether the research programmes behind the ontologies it reuses are still running; whether its own extension terms are published so anyone can look them up; and which kinds of knowledge an abundance of information leaves wanting. Each became askable only once consumer systems, ontology profiles and the field catalog existed to point at.
data.Name: Loop 15: The machinery around the knowledge: encoding technologies, funding programmes, published terms

data.Title: Controlled is not the same as secured: who reads the register in full
data.Premise: Loop 15's access-control seeding gave every governance table a policy, which silently retired the witness for 'access to process knowledge must be controlled': a column that asked whether a table had no policy at all now reads false everywhere. The question that only became askable once every table was policed is the sharper one -- of the policies that do exist, which ones cut no rows at all for a principal who is not an administrator. That condition is present in this model and an access review is exactly the exercise that looks for it.

schema.Description: The current reading of this question's predicates, extracted from the substrate after the loop ran: which witness columns fire, on how many rows out of how many. KnowledgeGaps has IdentifiedAt and a Status and computes no age, no ownership currency, and no relationship between a gap's severity and how long we have tolerated it. Known unknowns that never age are not being managed, they are being filed.

That ordering is fine. But nothing in the model checks the ordering, so an edit that PRECEDES no review and no change request looks identical to a governed one. Provenance of change is as much an epistemic question as provenance of belief.

data.QuestionText: Did we send an SMS to any recipient who had not given SMS consent at the moment we sent it?

Every SMS to a non-consenting recipient is an independent statutory violation with per-message damages, and the exposure scales with the size of the affected population. Right now the model cannot answer this at all -- there are no per-recipient send records -- so counsel cannot sign off on policy-04, cannot certify to an outside regulator, and cannot even scope the exposure. The absence of the record IS the legal problem: unanswerable and non-compliant look identical from the outside.

data.QuestionText: Did any SMS go out between 20:00 and 08:00 in the recipient's own local time?
data.WhyItMatters: comm-sms-policy declares QuietHoursStart 20:00 / QuietHoursEnd 08:00. Quiet-hours restrictions on non-emergency messaging are statutory in several jurisdictions and contractual in others, and a night-time text to an employee about an employment policy change is exactly the fact pattern that generates a complaint. The window wraps midnight, which is where naive implementations quietly get it wrong -- and a witness that is wrong in the safe direction is worse than no witness, because it manufactures false assurance.

data.QuestionText: For every recipient we could not reach, did we correctly refrain from marking their acknowledgement complete?
data.WhyItMatters: exc-unreachable is explicit: create an HR case, route to the manager, and do NOT mark acknowledgement complete. A falsely-recorded acknowledgement is the single most dangerous artifact in this entire model -- it is an affirmative written misrepresentation that the employee received and accepted a policy change, and it is exactly the document that gets subpoenaed in a wrongful-termination or unpaid-notice claim. Deemed-acknowledgement by silence is not acknowledgement. I would rather have zero acknowledgements than one fabricated one.

data.QuestionText: Do we still hold the exact text of every message we sent, for the full 2555-day retention period the policy commits us to?
data.WhyItMatters: Both comm-sms-policy and comm-email-policy declare RetentionDays=2555 -- seven years. That is a commitment we made in writing, and in a dispute the question is never 'what did the template say', it is 'what did THIS employee actually receive'. Templates contain variable substitutions; the rendered text is the evidence. If a delivery record exists but its rendered body is empty, we have a receipt with no document behind it, and the adverse inference runs against us.

data.QuestionText: Did any SMS we sent exceed 160 characters or split into more than 3 segments?

An over-length SMS silently splits at the carrier, arrives out of order, and -- this is the part that actually hurts -- the opt-out language is in the LAST segment, so an over-length message can strip the STOP instruction off the end of what people actually read. I have the template body and I have the policy limit sitting in the same rulebook and nothing compares them. This is the most embarrassing category of failure because it was computable from data we already had.

A status string with no approver behind it is not an approval, it is a claim. I need to be able to point at a row and say 'that is my name, that is the timestamp, that is the version of the text I saw'. Otherwise when something goes out wrong, 'approved' means nothing and the accountability lands wherever it lands.

data.QuestionText: Did every SMS we actually transmitted carry the approved opt-out text?
data.WhyItMatters: comm-sms-policy RequiredContent says 'Short notice, secure link, approved opt-out text' and the approved template ends with 'Reply STOP to opt out of SMS; email notices continue.' The opt-out is not decoration -- it is the mechanism by which consent stays meaningful, and it is the thing that gets clipped first when a message runs long. I want to check the RENDERED body, not the template, because that is what the employee saw. A policy that declares RequiredContent and never verifies it is a policy that documents an intention.

data.QuestionText: Loop 1 reports IsOverdueForReview=6/7, and I do not trust the number. It is computed from AgeDays, which is DATETIME_DIFF from ValidFrom — the date the claim became true, not the date anybody last looked at it. A fragment reviewed and reaffirmed last week reads exactly as overdue as one nobody has opened since it was written. I need the date of the last actual review recorded as a fact.
data.WhyItMatters: This is structural debt, and it is the kind that produces a plausible-looking wrong answer rather than an error. ValidFrom is a bitemporal validity bound; LastReviewedAt is a stewardship event. Deriving the second from the first is a category error that makes 6/7 unfalsifiable — there is no data that could make it read 5/7. The honest fix is a raw LastReviewedAt column, with the old inference retained as an explicit fallback-free comparison so the discrepancy itself becomes visible.

data.QuestionText: policy-08 makes me responsible for collecting acknowledgements, not just for transmitting. Five of six delivered messages have no acknowledgement. What have I actually done about that, and at what point does it become my unfinished work rather than the recipient's silence?
data.WhyItMatters: This is the half of my role I have been treating as somebody else's. My gates are elaborate and end the instant the message leaves. But policy-08 is assigned to me, and it says collect acknowledgements and exceptions -- an obligation with no gate, no witness, and until loop 1 built MessageDeliveries.IsAcknowledged, no observable state at all. IsAcknowledged=1/6 is the measurement of my post-send conduct and it is poor. A pipeline that transmits perfectly and then abandons the follow-up has automated the easy half and left the accountable half undone, while every dashboard reports the easy half. I want the reminder obligation computed the same way the send gates are: as a state I am in, with a clock on it, that I cannot satisfy by doing nothing.
data.Name: notification-publisher: policy-08 makes me responsible for collecting acknowledgemen

data.QuestionText: The event log from the ERP shows close-v1.1.0 running with 8 discovered variants and only 3 conforming — has anyone recorded that the live procedure and the live system actually disagree?
data.WhyItMatters: Every other witness in this model reasons from documents we wrote (StepTransitions, Requirements) or claims someone told us (KnowledgeFragments). None of them ever check what the system of record actually did. Process mining is a third, independent kind of evidence, and until now there was no table letting 'what we mined' contradict 'what we modeled' — a live version could drift from its own StepTransitions and nothing here would ever notice.

data.QuestionText: This rulebook compiles into Postgres, Python, Go, TypeScript, C#, a spreadsheet and an OWL reasoner. When I approve a rule, do all of them compute the same answer, and if not, which one is wrong about which field?
data.WhyItMatters: A procedure is only as authoritative as the systems that execute it. If the spreadsheet a controller opens disagrees with the database the close automation reads, the rule has two meanings, and nobody finds out until an audit does. Agreement has to be witnessed per cell, not assumed from a green build.
data.AnswerableBefore: No. The harness printed scores to a markdown file per substrate; the rulebook had no record of which substrates exist, how they scored, or which fields they disagree on.

data.QuestionText: Which steps can a procedure send work back to after they have already run — which steps sit on a rework loop, and which of those carry a blocking control that must hold on every pass?
data.WhyItMatters: Fallback and Alternative transitions make the step graph cyclic: close-04 falls back to close-03, and close-06's alternative re-enters close-04, so close-05's approval control can run twice in one close. Every witness we have looks at one transition at a time (IsUnwalkedRecoveryPath asks whether that one edge was ever traversed). None of them can say that a step is re-entered, because loop membership is reachability over paths of any length. That is transitive closure, which no formula expresses, so it needs the substrate-native closure over StepTransitions.

data.QuestionText: Can a procedure reach a publication step from its first step without passing through a human approval gate — is there any route, including alternative and fallback transitions, around the sign-off?
data.WhyItMatters: The CFO's sign-off at close-06 is only a control if every route to publication runs through it. IsHumanApprovalGate and GateHeldByHuman say the gate exists and is held by a person; nothing says the step graph forces work through it. An Alternative transition added for an 'immaterial variance' fast path can route straight to publication, and every per-step and per-edge witness stays green. Whether a gate can be bypassed is reachability from the entry step over only the transitions that avoid a gate, at any depth: a closure over a filtered edge set, not a formula.

data.QuestionText: An abundance of information still leaves three things wanting -- human judgment, the tacit knowledge nobody has uncovered yet, and knowledge curated to a particular person and task. For each of them, does this model hold anything, or does it only name the problem?
data.WhyItMatters: It is easy to build a system that is full of information and still cannot supply the three things people actually come to it for. I want each of the three named explicitly and pointed at the rows that answer it, so a gap shows up as an empty table rather than as an unexamined assumption.

data.QuestionText: Which of the vocabularies we depend on came out of a funded research programme, has that programme ended, and has anyone here been named to maintain what we took from it?
data.WhyItMatters: Ontologies for industry are largely produced by time-limited funded projects. When the funding ends the terms stay in our model and the maintainers go home. I need to see, before that happens, which of our dependencies are in that position and which of them nobody here has taken responsibility for.
